roadmap_item: §3 area I, Next 3: the model's second targets as a shortlist, held against an independent perturbation
question: Is a compiled element's second or further target at the compiler's bar (a protein-coding gene whose predicted change on deletion reaches enhancer_target.MIN_EFFECT, 0.1 log2, other than the compiled target; targetchoice.CANDIDATES, nothing re-tuned) more often a measured hit in Gasperini et al. 2019's at-scale K562 CRISPRi screen than the genes the same screen tested at the same element, at a matched distance, that the shortlist does not name, on the screen's tests that the CRISPRi benchmark does not hold?
shortlist: for each compiled element (the compiled programme with its experimental rule lines removed, signaltrace.PREDICTED_ONLY), the genes targetchoice.chromosome_choice lists as its candidate targets other than its compiled target(s), ranked as listed (strongest predicted change first): its second and further targets at the compiler's bar. Read as built by targetchoice; no parameter of it is set here
population: the at-scale screen's tests in its pair table (GSE120861_gene_gRNAgroup_pair_table.at_scale), one per candidate-enhancer guide group 'top_two' and gene, lifted from hg19 to GRCh38 by measured_unknown.Chain at liftOver's default (95% of bases); excluded and counted: non-targeting groups, TSS and other control groups, the 'second_two' repeat groups, elements the design labels not_model_selected_* (entered because a pilot screen found a hit there), tests that do not lift, and repeated tests. Then INDEPENDENCE. Then the gene must be protein-coding in GENCODE v50 by its Ensembl id, and the element must overlap at least one compiled element (half-open, one base)
independence: a test is excluded, and counted, when any row of either EPCrisprBenchmark file (training_K562 and heldout_5_cell_types, every dataset and cell type, read by coordinates, gene and dataset only) names the same gene (Ensembl id without version, or symbol) at an element overlapping the test's lifted element by at least one base. The remaining tests are independent of the benchmark pair by pair; the subset whose element overlaps no benchmark element at all is independent element by element and is read beside the primary

arms.compiled_target: the gene is a compiled target of an overlapping compiled element
arms.shortlist: the gene is a second or further candidate target of an overlapping compiled element and the compiled target of none; its rank is its best position among the candidates (2 = second)
arms.other: the gene is on no overlapping compiled element's candidate list

matching: each shortlist test is matched to every 'other' test of the same guide group (the same element) whose distance (hg19 |TSS - element midpoint|, from the pair table, at least 1 bp) is within a factor of DISTANCE_FACTOR of the shortlist gene's; its control rate is the share of those controls that are screen hits. A shortlist test with no such control is unmatched and counted. The nearest gene of the test's element is the independent protein-coding gene the screen tested there at the smallest distance (ties to the smaller Ensembl id), whatever its arm
hit_rule: a test is a screen hit when the readout table's empirical p-value adjusted by the screen (pvalue.empirical.adjusted) is below 0.1 and its fold change (fold_change.transcript_remap) is below 1: the screen's own call, a decrease. Rows join on the pair id 'gRNAgroup:ENSG' (pairs4merge, else pairs). A test with no readout row or a missing value is not measured: a shortlist test not measured leaves the comparison, a control not measured leaves its control set, and a shortlist test left with no measured control leaves; all counted
metric: over the matched shortlist tests that remain: the shortlist's hit rate minus the mean of their control rates, in percentage points, with a 95% interval from BOOTSTRAP (whole chromosomes resampled). Beside it and deciding nothing: the shortlist's rate minus the rate of the nearest gene at each test's element; the same difference on the element-independent subset; the compiled targets' rate at the same elements; the shortlist's rate by rank (2, 3, 4-5, 6+)

bootstrap.unit: chromosome (the matched tests of one chromosome are drawn together)

decision: TOO_FEW_PAIRS if fewer than MIN_MATCHED shortlist tests are matched (decided on the label-free census before any readout is opened); else NOT_RUN_NO_READOUT if the readout table is not on this machine; else HARNESS_DEFECT on any STOP_RULE condition; else, with [lo, hi] the 95% interval of the primary difference: MORE_OFTEN if lo > 0, LESS_OFTEN if hi < 0, otherwise NO_DIFFERENCE; TOO_FEW_PAIRS as well if fewer than MIN_MATCHED matched tests remain measured under HIT_RULE. The prediction holds on MORE_OFTEN only. The falsifier is NO_DIFFERENCE or LESS_OFTEN: then second targets were not detected to be measured hits more often than distance-matched genes the shortlist does not name. No margin beyond the interval is applied
stop_rule: one run, from this registration's committed code, on the files it pins by sha256. Nothing registered is changed after a readout value is read; a defect found afterwards is reported beside the reading and corrected only under a new registration. If the readout table's header lacks a registered column the run stops before any value is read, and a registration amendment changing column names only, committed before any value is read, is the one change allowed. The run stops with HARNESS_DEFECT before any test pair's readout is read if: a pinned input moved; the matched shortlist tests' ids or sha256 differ from the registration's; or, read first, fewer than POSITIVE_CONTROL_MIN of the screen's TSS guide groups are hits against the gene whose TSS they target (the readout is then being read wrongly)

outcomes.TOO_FEW_PAIRS: too few independent pairs: of the at-scale screen's {total} candidate-enhancer tests in K562, {excluded} are already in the CRISPRi benchmark (the same gene at an overlapping element) and {independent} are independent; {coding} of those test a protein-coding gene at an element that overlaps a compiled element, {short} of them a second or further target, and {matched} of those have a non-shortlist gene at a matched distance at the same element, fewer than the {min} the registered test needs; no readout was read
outcomes.NOT_RUN_NO_READOUT: not run, too few independent pairs with a readout: 0 of the {matched} independent Gasperini 2019 K562 tests of a second or further target that have a distance-matched control at the same element carry a readout on this machine, because the screen's differential-expression table ({readout}) was never fetched; {excluded} of the screen's {total} candidate-enhancer tests were excluded as already in the CRISPRi benchmark, {independent} are independent, {coding} of those test a protein-coding gene at a compiled element and {short} a second or further target. The registered test waits on that one table; nothing was read
outcomes.HARNESS_DEFECT: stopped before any test pair's readout was read: {what}
outcomes.MORE_OFTEN: second targets were measured hits more often: of {n} independent Gasperini 2019 K562 tests of a second or further target of a compiled element, {h} ({r}%) are screen hits, against {rc}% for the genes the screen tested at the same element at a matched distance that the shortlist does not name, {d} percentage points [95% CI {lo}, {hi}]; the nearest tested gene at those elements is a hit for {rn}%, {dn} points from the shortlist [95% CI {nlo}, {nhi}]. A screen hit is a measured decrease in K562, not function elsewhere
outcomes.NO_DIFFERENCE: no difference detected: of {n} independent Gasperini 2019 K562 tests of a second or further target of a compiled element, {h} ({r}%) are screen hits, against {rc}% for the genes the screen tested at the same element at a matched distance that the shortlist does not name, {d} percentage points [95% CI {lo}, {hi}]; the nearest tested gene at those elements is a hit for {rn}%, {dn} points from the shortlist [95% CI {nlo}, {nhi}]. No difference detected is not no difference
outcomes.LESS_OFTEN: second targets were measured hits less often: of {n} independent Gasperini 2019 K562 tests of a second or further target of a compiled element, {h} ({r}%) are screen hits, against {rc}% for the genes the screen tested at the same element at a matched distance that the shortlist does not name, {d} percentage points [95% CI {lo}, {hi}]; the nearest tested gene at those elements is a hit for {rn}%, {dn} points from the shortlist [95% CI {nlo}, {nhi}]

limitations: the benchmark kept the screen's pairs that passed its own filters (power, expression, distance), so the independent remainder is what those filters left out: on average less well powered, so its hit rates are lower than the benchmark's and a difference is harder to detect. Both arms share that

the shortlist names genes AlphaGenome predicts to respond, and a gene that responds in a predicted track is likely expressed; a single-cell readout detects a change more easily in a well-expressed gene. The matched control shares the element and the distance, not the expression level
AlphaGenome was trained on ENCODE data that include K562; the screen itself is not in its training as far as this lane knows, but its cell line is
a screen hit is a measured decrease of a gene's RNA in K562 after CRISPRi at the element; it is not function in another cell and not a mechanism
the screen's coordinates are hg19 and are lifted; distances are read in hg19 from the screen's own table
the design's selection label (general_group) is read only to exclude elements selected for a pilot hit; its other labels may encode pilot-screen status and are not used
descriptives_not_verdicts: the shortlist genome-wide: compiled elements, those with at least one second target, and the size of each element's shortlist
every exclusion count, the independence split (same gene in the benchmark, element in the benchmark for another gene, element not in the benchmark) and the benchmark datasets the excluded tests match
per arm: tests, elements, and (after the readout) hits; unmatched shortlist tests; the shortlist by rank
independence_check: the CRISPRi benchmark the project uses DOES include Gasperini 2019: its training file (EPCrisprBenchmark training_K562) carries 5,299 Gasperini2019 K562 rows of its 10,356, and its held-out file carries none. Of the at-scale screen's 128,962 candidate-enhancer tests (guide group top_two), 187 are on elements selected for a pilot hit and 38 do not lift, leaving 128,737; 6,015 of those name the same gene at an element overlapping a benchmark row (5,466 through Gasperini2019 rows alone, 549 through other datasets or several), and are excluded. 122,722 are independent pair by pair: 64,574 on an element the benchmark tested against another gene and 58,148 on an element it never tested. The screen's readout for them is not on this machine
prediction: a second or further target of a compiled element is more often a screen hit than the genes the screen tested at the same element at a matched distance that the shortlist does not name
baselines: distance-matched non-shortlist genes at the same element (the primary comparison)
the nearest tested protein-coding gene at the same element (read beside, decides nothing)
falsifier: NO_DIFFERENCE or LESS_OFTEN: second targets were then not detected to be measured hits more often than distance-matched genes the shortlist does not name
exploration_preceded_this: stated so that nothing here is read as blind to what this lane saw. Before writing this file the lane read: the at-scale pair table's header (12 columns, no effect, p-value or call column), five non-targeting rows and three candidate rows; counts of its guide-group suffixes and of its selection labels (general_group), which include labels ending '-hit' (5,620 rows 'test_5k-hit', 374 'not_model_selected_K1119hit-hit') that may mark pilot-screen hits by element; they are used only for the registered exclusion of not_model_selected_*. Counts of the benchmark files' rows by dataset, cell type and ValidConnection. An exploratory overlap count that also included the 'second_two' groups (7,492 of 138,057 tests the same gene at an overlapping benchmark element). The first lines of one ENCODE CRISPRi-FlowFISH element-quantification table (ENCFF005IVC.tsv, to learn its columns), which displayed one PPIF row's effect size; FlowFISH is not used here. Then, after MIN_MATCHED, DISTANCE_FACTOR, the hit rule and the outcomes were written, one dry run of this registration's label-free census (the counts registered below); after it one census key was renamed and nothing else changed. No Gasperini readout was read: the readout table is not on this machine. This lane did not read the benchmark's Regulated, Significant or EffectSize columns; the project has read the benchmark's Gasperini2019 labels in training for weeks, which is why those tests are excluded
departures: the independent population is what the benchmark's filters left out of the screen (power, expression, distance), not a random sample of the screen; LIMITATIONS says what that does to power

the hit rule's column names are those of the published readout table as this lane recalls them; the table is not on this machine to check, so a header that differs stops the run before any value is read, and a column-name-only amendment is the one change STOP_RULE allows

the nearest-gene baseline is the nearest independent protein-coding gene the screen tested at the element, which may be a compiled target or a shortlist gene itself; it is read beside the primary and decides nothing
the shortlist is targetchoice's candidate list as committed; the matching is within the same element, so the element's own activity is shared by the shortlist test and its controls

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record d365cdd

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
